criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the numbered decisions against the code paths and found one direct contradiction: missing page ids are skipped instead of hard-failing (Decision 1). The rest of the role-writing and brief-isolation logic largely matches the spec, including page-id keying, no title fallback, and the job-lens filters, so this is a pass-line artifact but not clean.

All required moving parts are present: the new spec, the graph writer, the retrieval filter, the migration, and selftests. The main gap is the seed-company count behavior: the SQL/render path does not guarantee a line for companies with zero role_posted rows, which leaves part of Decision 5 unfulfilled.

File placement and naming look in-family: project skill under .claude/skills/ has no alex: prefix, the spec/reference/doc updates are in the expected locations, and the new verb wiring follows existing patterns. I did not find a house-convention violation that clearly breaks the documented rules.

The patch stays fairly lean: it reuses ensure_event, avoids bespoke writers, and adds only the minimum isolation/filtering needed. There is some added caching/state (`_rcache`) and a new migration, but they look justified rather than duplicated platform work.

Diagnostics are generally strong: refusal paths are explicit, the new verb has selftests, and the pack path reports which isolation mode ran. Error messages are specific enough to explain failures. I did not see an opaque/silent failure mode in the new code.

defects.description: The spec says a role_posted manifest with no page id is a hard failure. This code returns a skip reason and lets ensure_roles continue, so the required failure is downgraded into a counted skip instead of stopping the write path.

defects.quote: select c.id as company_id, c.name, count(distinct e.id) as roles,
defects.description: The spec calls for one count line per seed company. This CTE only emits companies that already have role_posted rows, so a seed company with zero roles disappears entirely instead of showing a zero-count line.
